sysex.notes: Vendor SysEx (F0 47 7F 15 ...) is used for the LCD text display and global configuration (aftertouch mode, Live/User mode force). Normal pad/button/encoder operation in User Mode doesn't depend on it; the LCD is the only feedback that has no Note/CC alternative.

unresolved.reason: The device exposes a second port pair, 'Ableton Push Live Port', used for Ableton's own internal Live control-surface protocol. Neither mapping doc covers it, and it's out of scope for a User Mode profile, so it isn't modeled as a DevicePortProfile at all here.

unresolved.path: setup / handshake (no Device Inquiry reply observed)
unresolved.reason: Unlike the Launchpad, Push 1's User Port was not tested against a standard MIDI Universal Device Inquiry (F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7); neither mapping doc documents one, and sending one wasn't part of this verification pass. No handshake/setup is recorded in this profile; the device's identity above comes from its CoreMIDI port name, not a protocol-level reply.

Every pad also sends Poly Pressure (0xAn) by default, or Channel Pressure (0xDn) after the aftertouch-mode SysEx -- confirmed hands-on -- but PhysicalControl models one input address per control, so this second, mode-dependent input signal on the same physical pad has nowhere to go in this schema. Not represented.

The mapping doc's color table (section 5) gives three velocity values per color (bright/standard/dim- or pulse-animated); only the 'standard' column was sent and visually confirmed. PhysicalControl.feedback models one representative address per control (paletteSize 128), the same simplification the Launchpad profile already made for its own multi-mode color feedback -- the other two columns aren't separately modeled.

The mapping doc calls the physical User button 'hardcoded, unmappable' -- it switches the whole device between Live and User mode rather than reporting a note/CC -- and, separately and without realizing it was the same control, also (wrongly) labeled this exact CC 'Session' (round 2: lighting CC 59 showed 'User' printed on it). Not modeled as a PhysicalControl; its press itself was not independently tested (pressing it would have dropped the User Port mid-session), only its LED/label.

Round 2 only re-checked the specific buttons the original doc got wrong in its 'Bottom & Layout Selection Blocks'/'Right Column' sections; CC 34/35 ('Select'/'Shift') are from a different section of the same doc and weren't individually re-read off the hardware. Given that doc's now-demonstrated unreliability nearby, and that CC 49 is independently confirmed 'Shift' too (both can't be right), treat both labels as unconfirmed.

unresolved.path: controls (CC 113, CC 116, and an unlabeled block right of the pad grid)
unresolved.reason: Julien Bayle's diagram shows CC 113 as a real button (part of the Devices/Browse/Track/Volume/Pan-Send block) and a block of paired buttons right of the pad grid (roughly CC 48-57, 60-63), neither labeled in the diagram. The original mapping doc's CC 116 'Track' claim is now known wrong (the real Track is CC 112) and its function is unknown. None of these were tested; the real Mute/Solo/Clip-equivalent buttons the original doc misplaced at CC 49/50/112 likely live somewhere in this unlabeled block, unconfirmed.

The mapping doc documents SysEx to force Live or User mode outright (F0 47 7F 15 62 00 01 {00|01} F7). Not sent during verification, deliberately -- forcing Live mode would have dropped the User Port mid-session with no easy way back without touching the physical hardware.

Manufacturer/model aren't stated by either mapping doc (no manufacturer byline at all). Taken from the device's own CoreMIDI port names observed during verification ('Ableton Push Live Port' / 'Ableton Push User Port'), which is how the connected hardware actually identifies itself to the host OS -- not a SysEx Device Inquiry reply (Push 1 User Mode was not observed to answer one; see unresolved).

Confirmed directly: the device exposes exactly two duplex CoreMIDI ports, 'Ableton Push Live Port' and 'Ableton Push User Port'. Every verification test below ran against the User Port with the hardware in User Mode (physical User button held). The Live Port's own protocol (Ableton's internal Live-control surface scheme) was not investigated -- out of scope for User Mode profiling -- so only the User Port is modeled here.

The mapping doc's ASCII grid (section 3) states the full 8x8, bottom-left-origin, row-major note layout (notes 36-99). Only 4 of 64 pads were pressed directly (36, 37, 38, 46); the rest follow the same confirmed arithmetic pattern, not independently tested pad-by-pad.

Manufacturer id bytes (47 7F) and the LCD display message formula (F0 47 7F 15 {lineId} 00 45 00 [68 chars] F7) confirmed by sending real text to all 4 lines and visually reading it off the hardware. The aftertouch mode-force message (F0 47 7F 15 5C 00 01 {00|01} F7) also confirmed: it switched pad pressure between Poly and Channel Pressure as documented.
